name: Go Fashion (India) Ltd
title: Go Fashion (India) Ltd - 543401 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Go Fashion is shutting small EBOs and pivoting to 700+ sq ft stores while SSSG is negative (~-3%) and Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 25.3%; management guides no degrowth and margin recovery only from Q2, with no numeric guidance.

summary.headline: Go Fashion Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR196 crore with EBITDA margin at 25.3%; management guides FY27 SSSG positive and margin recovery from Q2.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR196 crore, gross margin 62.9%, EBITDA INR50 crore (25.3% margin) and PAT INR8 crore, with FY26 revenue at INR838 crore and PAT at INR59 crore. Full-year FY26 pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin was 11.5% versus 16.8% in FY25, with EBITDA down about INR40 crore to INR96 crore. Management is closing small EBOs (50-plus in FY26, about 50 more in Q1 FY27) and shifting to 700-plus sq ft stores, while the LFS channel recovered from about minus 30% in Q3 to about minus 7% in Q4 after adjusting for a INR5 crore credit note. Same-store sales growth was negative for FY26 and management targets positive SSSG by end FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Net margin about 7% vs 11% in FY25 per analyst

segments.name: EBO (company-operated stores)
segments.commentary: Network about 800 stores; about 275 stores were SSSG-positive in Q4 (average about 10-11%), mostly 300+ sq ft. Reported FY26 SSSG negative (about minus 3 to 3.5% per analyst's read); about 100-plus stores below 300 sq ft remain to be migrated. Retail space grew 43,000 sq ft (11%) in FY26.

segments.name: LFS (large format stores / partner channel)
segments.commentary: Q3 FY26 hit by a partner pausing intake for about 45 days (about minus 30%). Q4 reported decline of about 15-16%; management says about minus 7% after adjusting for INR5 crore credit note under Ind AS 115.

segments.name: Daily Wear concept
segments.commentary: Pilot of 10 stores as of 31 March 2026; target 25-30 stores by end FY27. Management calls early unit economics healthy, but sell-through has only just begun to pick up and it contributed to higher inventory.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: First international store opened in the Middle East during FY26; unit economics under study, rollout to remain measured.

guidance_outlook: Positive SSSG targeted for FY27 (management suggests turning positive by mid-FY27 or at least by year end); no degrowth in FY27 revenue expected, though no numeric growth guidance given.
Retail square footage to grow at least 10-11% net in FY27; net store count not guided.
Gross margin to be maintained in the 62.5%-63.5% range; no expansion expected.
EBITDA margin recovery expected from Q2 FY27 once about 50 small stores close in Q1; Q1 margins to stay weak. Management declined to quantify recovery.
Blended ASP expected at INR800-900 in the short term; aim to keep bottom-wear ASP below INR1,000.
Inventory days (about 4 months) expected to return to about 3 months in FY27.
Plan to add 10-12 new products in FY27, including all-day pants and cloud pants; brand ambassador to join in June 2026.
capex_capacity: Store format shift to 700-plus sq ft EBOs; 50-plus small stores closed in FY26 and about 50 more planned in Q1 FY27 via consolidation of overlapping catchments.
Tail of about 100-plus stores below 300 sq ft to be migrated over a longer period; timing not given.
Store expansion focused on Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities; management aims to nearly double square footage over the next 5 years.
Only 10-15 new Daily Wear / larger stores expected in FY27 to add about 2-3% of square footage; bottom-wear space growth about 10%, about 12% including Daily Wear.
Working capital and internal cash flows to fund expansion; no capex figure disclosed.
demand_pricing: Management says overall demand is better than 6-12 months ago, citing positive commentary from peer retail and apparel companies in Q4.
Blended ASP about INR800-811; about 70% of products priced below INR1,000 (down from about 80% over four quarters); products above INR1,300 being introduced.
Analyst noted ASP up about 9% and volume per store down about 11-12%; management said bill counts have not fallen and customers are buying higher-value items.
Management says no discounting policy maintained through FY26, supporting gross margin.
Competition: analyst raised multi-brand platforms (Nykaa) growing faster; management says it is deepening bottom-wear and testing top-wear and menswear via the Daily Wear pilot.

qa_highlights.question: Excluding closed stores, what is SSSG for the remaining network?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported SSSG is based on stores live through the year; about 275 stores were SSSG-positive in Q4 at roughly 10-11% average, mostly 300+ sq ft stores. Management said about 200-210 of the positive stores are above 300 sq ft.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to softer bottom-wear sales and Daily Wear pilot stock; inventory at about 4 months, expected to normalise to 3 months in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin outlook given cotton price rally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects gross margin in the 62.5%-63.5% range, with no expansion, as the no-discount policy is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of the EBITDA margin decline and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-Ind AS full-year EBITDA margin 11.5% vs 16.8%; closing small stores should remove over INR25 crore of cost, with margin recovery from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue fall 10-15% in FY27 due to store closures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no degrowth is expected in FY27 and it expects to grow, though it gave no numeric guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the store format shift cannibalising small stores and improving unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said larger stores show deep cannibalisation of nearby small stores and that 700-plus sq ft stores should match or beat 300 sq ft unit economics.

risks_watch: Negative SSSG for FY26; the FY27 positive SSSG target depends on store-migration revenue transfer, which management could not time.
Q1 FY27 margin likely weak during the 50-store closure; Q2 recovery is unquantified.
LFS channel still declining after adjustments; recovery to be confirmed in Q1 FY27.
Inventory elevated at about 4 months; Daily Wear sell-through still early.
Volume per store reportedly down about 11-12% while ASP rose, which management attributed to higher ticket prices.
Possible cotton price rise pressure on gross margin, which management says it will hold within 62.5-63.5%.
Brand ambassador launch (June 2026) and Daily Wear rollout (25-30 stores by FY27 end) are execution items to track.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and margin recovery from Q2 FY27, but evasive on quantification: management repeatedly declined to give numeric guidance on net store additions, SSSG timing, margins and net profit. Defensive about volume trends and the negative SSSG, attributing them to store format and display issues.
key_quotes: So from a full year basis, if you see our EBITDA for the full year pre-Ind AS EBITDA is 11.5% and last year was 16.8%.
We have not moved and pivoted to discounting. We have kept our no-discounting policy intact.
From a 700 square feet store size, we are able to say that in the long-term future as well, we will not have a situation where the store has started turning out to be small for us.

adds.what: 10-12 Daily Wear / larger-format stores in FY27 (about 25-30 Daily Wear stores by end FY27 from 10-store pilot)
Retail square footage growth of at least 10-11% net in FY27 via Tier 2/3 store expansion and 700-plus sq ft EBO format shift
About 50 small EBOs to close in Q1 FY27 (consolidation of overlapping catchments)

growth.why: Management guides positive full-year SSSG by end FY27, no FY27 revenue degrowth, gross margin held at 62.5-63.5%, and at least 10% sq ft growth; no numeric revenue guidance, and backing is partial (store adds and 10-12 new products, but no capex figure and no quantified margin recovery).
